entities.summary: Brice of Tours (b. 377 CE, Touraine) was a prominent religious figure and entrepreneur of the Classical era, active in Touraine and known for his business acumen and faith-based initiatives. He played a key role in the development of Christianity in Gaul, working closely with the early Christian church and its leaders. Brice's entrepreneurial spirit and religious convictions led to the establishment of various Christian institutions and businesses in the region, which would later become a model for future religious organizations. His legacy can be seen in the continued presence of Christianity in France and the impact of his business ventures on the local economy. According to the Vita S. Bricii, Brice was a devoted follower of Saint Martin of Tours, and his faith was a driving force behind his work. Brice's story serves as a testament to the enduring power of faith and entrepreneurship in shaping the course of human history.
